question: What can a precisely specified computation accomplish?
idea: Some mathematical questions concern whether a procedure exists at all; others concern how much time or how accurate an approximation it needs. Those are different limits. This entry studies the particular computational question stated below.
why: Mathematics used to understand physical models, including quantum systems and interacting particles. A theorem concerns a specified model, not every physical situation.

glossary.meaning: A rational number is a number that can be written as a fraction of two integers.
A way of measuring the number of independent directions or degrees of freedom; different theories use different notions.

exactClaim: Proves QMA-hardness of approximating the electronic Coulomb energy infimum in three dimensions, minimizing over the full spinful fermionic continuum space. Deterministic polynomial-time reductions work even with only unit-charge nuclei at distinct rational positions, polynomially many electrons and an energy-threshold separation of at least one.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
